_what: Coverage sweep of 2026-08-26: every rank ordering and distance-chain variant that had never been rendered live. Planned by scripts/coverage_sweep_plan.py from scripts/render_coverage.py's gap list.
result: 71 columns, 71 headers, 0 mismatches against omega.fanout.outputs_for. Every header also appeared in conditionColumns, so none tripped the duplicate-header section-drop.

orderingAliases.what: For a metric whose values are all one sign, two of the four orderings are the SAME column under different names. Measured, not reasoned: BTC OI_rank_lo and OI_rank_near are both 78/78; RVOL_rank_lo == RVOL_rank_near (61/78); highDev_rank_lo == highDev_rank_near (39/78); dist_swingLo_rank_lo == dist_swingLo_rank_near (30/78 BTC, 20/78 ETH). And for a never-positive metric it is lo == far instead: lowDev_rank_lo == lowDev_rank_far (38/78).
orderingAliases.rule: non-negative metric -> rank_lo is rank_near, and rank_hi is rank_far. non-positive metric -> rank_lo is rank_far, and rank_hi is rank_near.
orderingAliases.consequence: Part of the operand-expanded shape count is semantic duplication rather than distinct capability. Authoring both members of an alias pair spends two of the 32 section-column slots on one measurement, and the headers differ so nothing warns you.
orderingAliases.affects: every rank over a single-signed metric - OI, OI_CHG, RVOL, VOLUME, TRADES, BUY_TRADES, SELL_TRADES, ATR, ATR_PCT, BB_WIDTH, BB_WIDTH_PCT, HIGH_DEV (never negative), LOW_DEV (never positive), and the dist_* chains whose sign is fixed by construction

rankScopingNote.what: Every response in this sweep carried a top-level `rankScopingNote`: 'Rank columns reflect the full active market, not the previewed coin selection - a coin may show a rank higher than the number of rows shown.'
rankScopingNote.significance: Column Algebra addendum item 8 recorded that the section preamble and conditionColumns described rank scoping two contradictory ways, and that the values agreed with conditionColumns (market-wide). The platform now states it explicitly at the top level. Values here confirm it: 2 coins previewed, ranks rendered as n/78.
rankScopingNote.status: Not re-verified as a fix - item 8's contradiction was between two OTHER fields, and this note is a third statement that happens to agree with the correct one. Recorded as an observation.

_naming: NOT named _renders*.json deliberately. omega.probe.load_all_renders() globs that prefix and requires each match to be a VERBATIM {capturedAt, request, response} capture; this file is a summary of headers and findings, so the prefix would break every consumer of the render caches. It did, briefly.
